I measure urban life with new forms of data, from WiFi signals to online reviews and listings, and test how well those measures hold up for policy.

-   **Public space & pedestrian behavior**: WiFi sensing and open-source measurement tools
-   **Commercial district change**: online reviews, sensory experience, and business continuity
-   **Housing markets & policy**: online listings, *jeonse*–monthly rent transitions, and household outcomes
-   **AI in urban research** *(exploring)*: LLM agents for simulating residents' responses to housing policy

## Software

**[urban-wifi-sensing-toolkit](https://juhyeonpark.com/urban-wifi-sensing-toolkit/){.ptitle}**: An open-source R toolkit for measuring pedestrian activity with WiFi sensing, from sensor assembly to urban analytics metrics. Includes sample data from two field deployments.
